title: ONE SMALL SUITCASE (THEY SAID)
route: London Heathrow → Lagos Murtala Muhammed Airport

shots.label: Hook
shots.on_screen_text: When family says 'just one small bag'...

lines.text: Dash. Dash. DASH. Auntie said one small suitcase. ONE. Why am I looking at three boxes, two coolers, and what I think is a FULL MATTRESS?
lines.speaker_context: eyes bulging wide, fur standing on end, spinning around in disbelief, gesturing wildly at a mountain of luggage that nearly touches the ceiling of his flat

lines.text: The mattress is a 'small item' according to your uncle. His words, not mine.
lines.speaker_context: calm deadpan smirk, leaning against the doorframe with tiny arms folded, sipping a cup of tea without a care in the world

shots.label: Problem
shots.on_screen_text: The family group chat has entered the chat.

lines.text: My phone is VIBRATING off the table — Mum wants stockfish, Cousin Temi wants six jars of Marmite, and Grandma is asking me to bring 'a little fresh air from London.' HOW?!
lines.speaker_context: phone buzzing violently in his paw, fur frazzled, reading notifications with escalating horror, one eye twitching

lines.text: To be fair, the Marmite I understand. The fresh air is ambitious.
lines.speaker_context: peering over at Bounce's phone screen, tiny eyebrow raised, expression perfectly dry and unimpressed

lines.text: Dash, we check in at SIX AM. We are going to get stopped. We are going to be that family at the airport. I cannot be that family!
lines.speaker_context: clutching his head with both paws, tail puffed up in full panic mode, dramatically sinking to the floor

shots.label: Tension
shots.on_screen_text: Heathrow security did NOT come to play.

lines.text: Right. Small update. I may be... detained at security.
lines.speaker_context: voice coming through a tiny earpiece, eerily calm considering the situation, whispering with the faintest trace of concern

lines.text: DETAINED?! Dash, what did you PUT in that bag?! I told you the pepper soup seasoning looked suspicious on an X-ray — I TOLD YOU!
lines.speaker_context: frozen mid-stride at the airport departure gate, orange fur bristling in all directions, paw pressed over his mouth, green eyes nearly popping out of his head, other passengers staring

lines.text: It is not the pepper soup. It is the stockfish. Apparently it has its own... atmosphere. The security owl is giving it a full investigation.
lines.speaker_context: small and composed inside a glass security booth, travel bag on the conveyor belt, watching a very serious uniformed owl in a hi-vis vest sniff the bag with intense professional suspicion

shots.label: Idea
shots.on_screen_text: BootHop to the rescue — no drama, no X-ray.

lines.text: Bounce. Listen. Next time — all of this? The boxes, the coolers, the Marmite, even Grandma's symbolic fresh air — goes through BootHop. Door to door, Lagos delivery, zero airport drama.
lines.speaker_context: reunited outside security, absolutely unruffled, holding up his phone showing the BootHop app interface, one small finger tapping the screen with quiet authority

lines.text: You mean I don't have to CHECK IN with a mattress?! I can just... send it? Like a normal person?!
lines.speaker_context: staring at Dash's phone with jaw dropped open, green eyes wide and glistening, one paw on his chest like a weight has been physically lifted off him

shots.label: Realisation
shots.on_screen_text: Lagos. The delivery arrives before they do.

lines.text: Dash. Dash. The BootHop parcel is already at Auntie's house. We just landed. How is it already THERE?!
lines.speaker_context: standing outside Lagos arrivals in the warm Nigerian sun, straw hat slightly askew, jaw hanging, holding his phone showing a delivery confirmed notification, absolutely delighted and baffled

lines.text: That is what happens when you stop arguing with airport scales and let the professionals handle it.
lines.speaker_context: pulling down tiny sunglasses onto his nose, travel bag slung over one shoulder, cool composed smile, the picture of effortless calm in the Lagos heat

lines.text: Bro. I am emotional. I am actually emotional right now.
lines.speaker_context: paw placed over his heart, eyes welling up with genuine moved-ness, bottom lip trembling in that big dramatic Bounce way, sunshine glowing on his orange fur

shots.label: Ending
shots.on_screen_text: One small suitcase. Delivered. No stress.

lines.text: Right. Next trip — I pack light, BootHop sends the madness ahead, and I arrive fresh. Like a KING.
lines.speaker_context: striking a triumphant pose outside arrivals, chest puffed, orange fur gleaming in the Lagos sun, sunglasses finally on, one paw pointing to the sky with absolute confidence

lines.text: You still told your auntie you'd bring the mattress IN PERSON. She's outside. She has a look.

caption: Auntie said 'one small suitcase.' Bounce showed up with a mattress. Dash had a better idea. 📦✈️ #BounceOnTheMove #BootHop
setting: London Heathrow Airport → Lagos Murtala Muhammed Airport, Nigeria
story_summary: Bounce is ambushed by his family's ever-expanding list of items to carry to Lagos — one small suitcase has become a mountain of boxes, coolers, and a mattress. At Heathrow, chaos erupts when Dash gets detained at security over suspicious stockfish, and Bounce nearly has a breakdown at the check-in desk. Dash reveals that BootHop could have handled all of it — door-to-door delivery to Lagos, no X-rays, no excess baggage fees, no drama — and when they land in Nigeria to find the parcel already delivered, Bounce is genuinely moved. The kicker: Auntie is still waiting for that mattress in person.
